reasoning: I was unable to locate any general-election polling or national forecaster ratings specifically for Hawaii’s 2024 or 2026 presidential or U.S. Senate races within the last 45 days; most recent coverage focuses on state legislative and congressional primaries, not on statewide federal matchups.[2][5][8][12][14][15] Given the absence of fresh race-specific data, the best available structural indicator is Hawaii’s strongly Democratic Partisan Voting Index (about D+14 statewide), which implies that any current Senate or presidential margin is very likely D+ in double digits even though no recent, state-specific public polls confirm an exact number.[3][7][11]

sources.name: Hawaii Office of Elections
sources.details: Hawaii Office of Elections provides procedural information and timelines for the August 8, 2026 primary election but does not discuss partisan advantages or general-election margins.

sources.name: Aloha State Daily
sources.details: Aloha State Daily summarizes 2026 Hawaii state Senate primary results, noting close races and higher primary turnout than 2024, but offers no general-election or federal race margins.

sources.name: New York Times
sources.details: New York Times reports primary results for Hawaii’s 2nd Congressional District, with Jill Tokuda winning the Democratic primary by overwhelming margins and county-level vote spreads, but it does not address statewide Senate or presidential general-election margins.

sources.name: PBS NewsHour
sources.details: PBS NewsHour provides live results and process details for Hawaii’s midterm primaries, including turnout and timing of vote updates, without expressing a partisan lean for statewide federal races.

sources.name: Hawaii Public Radio
sources.details: Hawaii Public Radio reports certified primary election results statewide and explains how and when results were released, but does not analyze party advantage in the upcoming general election.

sources.name: Honolulu Civil Beat
sources.details: Civil Beat reports that most Hawaii legislative incumbents won their primaries easily and includes a few district-level vote margins, but it does not extrapolate to statewide Senate or presidential race advantages.

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.details: Al Jazeera covers Hawaii primary results emphasizing that incumbents, including Democratic Rep. Ed Case, secured nominations, which implies Democratic strength in federal races but offers no quantified statewide margin.

sources.name: Hawaii Free Press
sources.details: Hawaii Free Press summarizes second-read primary results, including a tied GOP state Senate primary resolved by lot and turnout figures, but provides no general-election polling or statewide partisan rating.

sources.name: Cook Political Report
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s recent material explains and updates its Partisan Voting Index methodology and state scores, from which Hawaii’s approximate D+14 statewide PVI can be inferred as a structural indicator of strong Democratic lean rather than a current poll margin.
